title: Small domestic companies' beneficial ownership (BOI) reporting burden has been removed by FinCEN rulemaking

history.reason: Corporate Transparency Act reporting was widely expected to burden small companies.

FinCEN's March 2025 interim final rule exempted domestic reporting companies, and the August 2026 rule's background describes narrowing reporting to foreign companies; the compliance problem for small domestic companies is overtaken by events. Reopen if reporting is reinstated.

description: Small domestic companies were once required to file beneficial ownership reports with FinCEN; FinCEN's 2025 interim final rule excluded domestic companies from the reporting requirement.
context: Preserved as research history so the same dead end is not re-investigated; rule status after August 2026 not verified.

evidence.text: FinCEN's interim final rule effective March 26, 2025 exempts all domestic reporting companies and their beneficial owners from BOI reporting.
FinCEN's August 14, 2026 rule background states Treasury's intent to narrow reporting to foreign companies only.

contradictory_evidence.text: The August 2026 rule's operative provisions were not fully read, so reporting obligations for foreign companies or future reinstatement are not characterized here.

uncertainty: Unknown: operative text of the 2026 rule, litigation or legislative changes, and any state-level beneficial ownership requirements.
open_questions: Do state-level beneficial ownership or similar filings create a replacement problem?
next_actions: Reopen only if federal reporting for domestic companies is reinstated or state requirements emerge.
